title: noah-ramirez-private-deploy-scratchpad-2026-03-10
content:
Daily scratchpad - private deploy field notes (customer: AcmeHealth)
Date: 2026-03-10
Owner: Noah Ramirez

Context/goal:
- On-site prep for VPC + on-prem gateway install for AcmeHealth. Bring the minimal playbook to finish initial control-plane handshake and verify inference traffic over private network.

High-level checklist (today):
- [ ] Confirm customer VPC peering and route table entries (B2B peering w/ transit-gw).
- [x] Collect AWS account IDs and IAM ARNs from infra team (done 2026-03-09).
- [ ] Run initial kube-proxy & node readiness checks on customer cluster.
- [ ] Install edge-gateway helm chart (no-bastion flow).
- [ ] Validate TLS certs + KMS key access (bring fallback instructions).
- [ ] Smoke test: send sample inference payload through private endpoint and verify trace ID.
- [ ] Document any port/firewall rules customer must add to on-prem firewall.

Customer environment notes (from pre-call):
- Region: us-east-1 for control-plane endpoints; customer actually has primary DC in us-east-2 but will peer to us-east-1 transit gateway.
- VPC ids: <customer-vpc-1> (app), <customer-vpc-ops> (bastion/management) - confirm exact IDs on arrival.
- Subnets: uses /19 public/private mix. Have UX to suggest adding a /28 for edge gateway.
- KMS: AcmeHealth uses an HSM-backed key; we must request KMS grant principal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodPrivateDeployRole (placeholder).
- Egress rules: corporate firewall only allows 443 outbound to specific IPs; will need to add redwood control plane CIDRs (RFC: 34.200.100.0/24, placeholder) or proxy through customer-managed NAT.

Install steps (concise) - local notes for quick run:
1) Pre-reqs: kubectl context set to customer cluster, helm v3, jq, awscli + creds with STS assume-role to customer account.
2) Verify nodes: kubectl get nodes -o wide; kubectl describe node <node> if NotReady.
3) Create namespace redwood-private and apply resource quotas/limits: kubectl apply -f ns-quota.yaml.
4) Secrets: create TLS secret from provided certs: kubectl create secret tls redwood-edge-tls --cert=acme_edge.crt --key=acme_edge.key -n redwood-private.
5) KMS/GCP KMS: add KMS grant per playbook and verify with aws kms get-key-rotation-status.
6) Helm install edge gateway: helm upgrade --install redwood-edge ./charts/edge --namespace redwood-private -f values-acme.yaml --set controlPlane.endpoint=https://control.redwood.internal || capture logs (/tmp/edge-install.log).
7) Post-install checks: kubectl rollout status deployment/redwood-edge -n redwood-private; kubectl logs -l app=redwood-edge -n redwood-private --tail=200.
8) Connectivity test: curl -v --resolve edge.acme.internal:443:<edge-pod-ip> https://edge.acme.internal/healthz (expect 200).
9) Send smoke inference: curl -X POST https://edge.acme.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <test-token>' -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' and verify response and tracing headers X-Trace-Id.

Blockers / unknowns to resolve ASAP:
- Firewall/egress: Customer security team requires explicit IPs, they refused CIDR ranges in pre-call. Need to get list of NAT egress IPs or set up proxy. Action: ask Riley to surface NAT IPs from infra team (ticket JIRA-PDEP-1987).
- KMS grant TTL: unclear how long Acme will grant the KMS key; need to document rotation window. Action: confirm retention window with Samira.
- On-prem network team will not allow inbound from internet; we must ensure control-plane connections can originate from customer to Redwood (no inbound). Confirm if control-plane can be tunneled over customer-managed proxy.

Quick troubleshooting snippets:
- If helm install hangs on init-container: kubectl describe pod <pod> -n redwood-private; check init container logs: kubectl logs <pod> -c init -n redwood-private.
- Cert mismatch errors: curl --insecure -v to check server cert details, then openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -showcerts.
- KMS AccessDenied: aws sts get-caller-identity (validate assumed role); aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ciphertext.bin --key-id <key> to reproduce.

Customer-specific reminders (put in final runbook):
- Provide step-by-step NAT IP allowlist for customer firewall team.
- Add how-to for rotating KMS grants and expiring secrets.
- Include fallback: if direct KMS not allowed, use envelope encryption with customer-managed HSM + offline key exchange (requires legal).

Notes to self:
- Pack a small USB with offline copies of tls certs and playbook PDF.
- Bring laptop with both corp and customer VPN profiles; test both pre-boarding.
- Call with Acme infra at 09:30 local tomorrow to confirm route table updates.

Next actions (owning):
- Morning: get final VPC IDs and NAT IP list (owner: Noah, due: 2026-03-10 10:30).
- Midday: attempt helm install in staging mirror before touching prod cluster (owner: Riley).
- Afternoon: consolidate final notes into a cleaned runbook and upload to Confluence (owner: Noah/Samira, due: 2026-03-11).

Quick links:
- Confluence runbook (draft): CONF-PRIVATE-DEPLOY-42
- JIRA ticket: JIRA-PDEP-1987
- Ops PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/402

End of scratchpad. Will convert to formal runbook after site visit.
